content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Supply, not demand, is the problem. Both queues logged 7 sick absences against about 2.5 usual. Most notes say 'dengue fever' (4 in payments, 7 in general). Payments is short (27 vs 32.5 expected agents), and volume there is actually 9% below forecast. General volume is near forecast (+1.9%), and the small loan_enquiry rise is not material. The only incident is a resolved overnight batch delay. The only marketing send was a newsletter with no call-to-action. Since the 13:00 package (overtime, coaching cancelled, breaks delayed, callback, chat deflection), service level has recovered to about 95-100% on payments and about 77-98% on general.","plan_name":"Light top-up: cover evening sick gap within remaining budget","rationale":"Current levers have restored service level, so only the uncovered tail of the day needs action. Overtime and IVR callback currently run only to 17:00, and the sickness will persist into the evening. Six 8-agent, 2-hour overtime offers are already out. At about 40% acceptance that is roughly Rs 13,800 committed, leaving about Rs 1,200 of the Rs 15,000 budget. One small payments overtime offer for 17:00-19:00 (3 offered, about 1.2 accepted, about Rs 860) fits within that. Payments is the queue with the staffing alert. Free IVR callback on both queues 17:00-20:00 protects the 80/20 target against the sick shortfall without extra cost. More break delays would mostly skip agents already delayed today. Coaching is already cancelled to 20:00.
